newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-LAND SELL-OFF LAW UNDER PREPARATION.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-LAND SELL-OFF LAW UNDER PREPARATION.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said it hopes to see a general law on land privatisation passed before parliament begins its summer holidays in July, simplifying the procedure and determining the responsible state authorities.
The draft law provides for the LPA to be in charge of selling state land with buildings as well as land on which nothing is built in both cities and rural areas.

"The law, expected to be passed before the summer recess, will combine the current regulations on city land reform with the sale of rural lands," Viktor Shadinov, the LPA's legal manager, told a news conference.
"It will make the procedures quicker and simpler as well as determine which authority is responsible for which lands," he added.
Exceptions to the law will include forests. The LPA will only have the right to privatise forest land with buildings such as foresty facilities, Shadinov said.
There will be no first rights of refusal for land with no buildings on and most of it will be auctioned off, Shadinov said.
Land can be privatised for cash and property compensation vouchers. The later must be worth at least 50 percent of purchase prices.
